text:
For an iPhone 17, my top pick is the **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)**. If you want faster charging and more capacity, I'd choose the **INIU SnapGo Air 10K**.

## Top picks

**Best overall slim: Anker Nano Power Bank 5K, about $55**
- It's 0.34 in thick, weighs 4.3 oz and has 5,000mAh. It charges at 15W through Qi2 and is listed as a fit for the iPhone 17 series.
- 9to5Mac says it feels premium and runs cooler than the competition. It also calls it the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery.
- [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank). Details are from the [Anker page](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank) and [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/).

**Best slim with fast charging: INIU SnapGo Air 10K, about $43 to $49**
- It has 10,000mAh and is about 0.5 in thick and 195g, which is slim for its capacity. Macworld lists it as tied for the slimmest 10K power bank.
- It charges your iPhone 17 wirelessly at 25W (Qi2.2) and over a cable at 45W. It includes a lanyard-style 60W cable and has a digital display but no kickstand.
- It's roughly twice the thickness of the Anker, but you get about twice the capacity.
- Sources: [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge) and [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html). Android Central lists it at Amazon and INIU, but I don't have a direct product link.

## Other options

- **Thinnest and lightest: Baseus Picogo Air AM71 (5K).** It's 0.27 in thick and 104g, but wireless charging tops out at 7.5W. It's about $53 at Amazon, per [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge).
- **Slim with 15W wireless: ReelCharge ReelSafe (5K).** It's 0.35 in thick and 119g, uses a semi-solid-state battery and costs about $50. See the same Android Central review.
- **Tougher 10K: TORRAS MiniMag Pro.** It's 0.57 in thick, has an IP54 dust and water rating, and charges wirelessly at 15W. It costs about $70 to $80, per the same review.
- **If thickness matters less: Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10K, 25W Qi2.2, 45W wired).** It's about $54 after code AM52, per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w). [Buy at Baseus](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w). That is an affiliate link, and I couldn't find its thickness in the results.

## Things to know
- 5K models give roughly 60 to 75% of an iPhone charge. 10K models give close to two full charges, according to Macworld.
- 25W Qi2.2 works only on the iPhone 16 and later, so your iPhone 17 qualifies. 15W models are fine for most top-ups.
- Thick or non-magnetic cases can weaken the connection. Anker advises cases under about 2.5 mm.
- Prices change often, so check the current price at checkout.

For the thinnest possible bank, get the Anker. For an all-day battery that still isn't bulky, get the INIU.
